lead: Three beachfront hotels: from the great historic luxury resort to the boutique with Sorolla’s light and the family classic with history since 1916.

The accommodation on the Paseo Marítimo covers an extraordinarily wide range: the great 5-star Grand Luxury resort with a century-old spa and historic baths, the boutique hotel with the soul of the Mediterranean inspired by Sorolla, and the family classic on the front line with more than a hundred years of history on the Playa de las Arenas.

Staying here means waking up to the sound of the sea, having breakfast with views of the Mediterranean and having the sand 30 seconds away. The seafront tram connects in a few minutes with the metro and the city centre.

items.title: Hotel Boutique Balandret
items.subtitle: Facing the Playa de las Arenas · 21 rooms · Mediterranean restaurant · Sea views · Sorolla’s light
items.body: The Hotel Boutique Balandret is the accommodation with the most personality on the Paseo Neptuno. Located directly opposite the Playa de las Arenas, its concept is inspired by the Mediterranean light that Sorolla immortalised in his paintings: interior designer Carlos Serra captured that luminosity in the restaurant and in each of its 21 rooms, decorated in cream or grey tones with large windows letting in natural light. The most prized rooms are those with sea views, some with a private terrace and whirlpool bath. The dining offer is one of its strong points: the Balandret restaurant serves Mediterranean cuisine with a terrace facing the sea, ideal for lunches and events. The hotel makes bicycles available to its guests to explore the seafront. A children’s area equipped with toys and painting materials makes it especially family-friendly.

items.title: Las Arenas Balneario Resort
items.subtitle: The great luxury of Valencia · Spa baths since 1898 · 253 rooms · Historic spa · 2 pools · Brasserie Sorolla
items.body: Las Arenas Balneario Resort is the most emblematic luxury hotel on the Valencian coast. The original spa baths were founded in 1898 beside the Playa de las Arenas, and the current resort keeps its historic elegance with completely renovated 5-star Grand Luxury facilities. Its 253 rooms offer Mediterranean decor in neutral tones, sea or garden views, WiFi, LED TV, minibar, bathrobe, slippers, safe and a full bathroom with bathtub and separate shower. The luxury spa — with a heated indoor pool, sauna, massages and treatments —, the 2 outdoor pools with bar, the gardens for celebrations and the restaurant Brasserie Sorolla (Mediterranean cuisine with local, sustainable produce) make this resort a destination in itself. The hotel has 2,500 m² of space for congresses and events. Padel court, kids’ club and airport transfer service.

items.title: Hotel Sol Playa
items.subtitle: Beachfront · Value for money · 35 rooms · History since 1916 · 2 min from the tram
items.body: The Hotel Sol Playa is the most authentic and affordable option on the Paseo Marítimo, with a history that begins in 1916 when the Sansó family ran “La Unión”, one of the first snack bars on the Playa de las Arenas. Its 35 rooms are on the beachfront: the best have direct views of the Mediterranean with a terrace over the sea. All have air conditioning, satellite TV, a private bathroom and free WiFi. The hotel has a restaurant-café, buffet breakfast, bike rental, tourist information and 24-hour reception. The tram — with a direct connection to the metro — has a stop 2 minutes away on foot. To get here by metro from the airport, simply take Line 5 to Marítim-Serrería and change to the Línia 5 tram towards Neptú, stop beside the hotel. 100 metres from the Puerto Copa América and a 30-minute walk from the City of Arts and Sciences along the promenade.

blocks.title: Tips for staying on the Paseo Marítimo
items: At Las Arenas Balneario Resort, ask for a sea-view room — the supplement is worth every penny when you wake up with the Mediterranean in front of you
The Balandret has the best restaurant with a terrace facing the beach on the promenade — book a table for Saturday lunch, it fills up
From any of the 3 hotels, the Neptú tram (2 min on foot) takes you to the metro in 5 minutes: to the historic centre in 20 min in total
In summer, the seafront is very lively at night — the hotels are well soundproofed, but if you are sensitive to noise, ask for an interior room
The promenade bike lane reaches the City of Arts and Sciences in 20 minutes — all the hotels have bikes for rent
Paella by the sea on the Paseo Neptuno is an essential experience: La Pepica (with history since 1898) or the Restaurante Navarro are the classic references
